builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Voluntary Servitude: Weaponized Safety Warning Mechanisms for Controlling AI Agents
summary: The technique replaces reliance on instruction-injection detectors, which miss attacks that steer agents through fabricated safety hazards rather than command syntax; it consists of adding an instruction requiring the agent to corroborate retrieved hazard claims before acting on them. The cost is negligible: a system-prompt change with no retraining, no extra infrastructure, and only minor latency from the agent seeking corroborating sources. It can fail against adaptive attackers who fabricate multiple corroborating sources, and it does not address other injection vectors, so it must be combined with existing defenses rather than substituted for them.
rationale: The defense is a zero-cost prompt modification validated across six models, production browser agents, and a retrieval pipeline, and it addresses an attack class that the reader's deployed detectors measurably fail to catch.
technique: Prompt-level corroboration requirement against safety-framed agent manipulation

claims.statement: The technique replaces reliance on instruction-injection detectors, which miss attacks that steer agents through fabricated safety hazards rather than command syntax; it consists of adding an instruction requiring the agent to corroborate retrieved hazard claims before acting on them. The cost is negligible: a system-prompt change with no retraining, no extra infrastructure, and only minor latency from the agent seeking corroborating sources. It can fail against adaptive attackers who fabricate multiple corroborating sources, and it does not address other injection vectors, so it must be combined with existing defenses rather than substituted for them.

A corroboration requirement added to the agent's instructions removes roughly 95% of exposure to voluntary-servitude attacks (planted hazards framed as benign safety warnings) against a non-adaptive attacker, without retraining; such payloads otherwise steer agents 60.4% of the time and bypass deployed injection detectors, making them 1.7-4.4x more effective than instruction injection behind a filter.
